patches.title: Keep native MCP access available during long active runs
patches.problem: New heartbeat_run MCP tokens expire after one hour even when an authorized run is still working.
patches.reason: The installed adapter exposes only an immutable getServers snapshot, and the public mint API rejects heartbeat_run. The operator selected a four-day default in this downstream fork.
patches.owner: Native run preparation and gateway-token lifecycle
patches.proposal: Issue assigned and managed run MCP gateway tokens with a 96-hour expiry. Preserve all existing per-call checks and terminal revocation. No renewal mechanism or permission expansion.
testsRequired: Both runtime issuing paths use 96 hours and retain authority
Missing or changed assignments do not mint credentials
patches.validation: Six focused offline source-function tests and the same six tests against the generated runtime passed. PostgreSQL integration coverage was updated but not run in the sparse checkout. The deployed runtime hash, exact version and commit were read back through authenticated health. No real task test was run.
patches.migration: No schema or data migration. Existing credentials retain their stored expiry and revocation.
patches.rollback: Activate the retained upstream payload; do not roll back the database or task evidence. Future minting uses upstream expiry; existing tokens still use native revocation.
patches.retireWhen: An upstream version provides equivalent active-run continuity, authority boundaries and terminal revocation, confirmed by the same regression cases.

patches.title: Make managed-update health verification compatible with authenticated instances
patches.problem: The CLI probes health without authentication but requires an exact version. Authenticated deployments intentionally omit version fields from anonymous healthy responses, causing a false rollback and false rollback-restart failure.
patches.reason: Liveness alone cannot prove the intended binary is active; protected details must not be made public to satisfy the updater.
patches.owner: Managed CLI service verification and authenticated health response contract
patches.proposal: Use an authorized local/admin health context for exact installed-version verification, retaining identity checks and redacted public liveness.
testsRequired: Authenticated healthy expected version succeeds without exposing protected fields
Wrong version, unavailable or unhealthy service still fails verification
Rollback verification uses the same authenticated contract
patches.validation: Source and deployment readback establish the mismatch; no source fix implemented. An idle-service native stop/update/start procedure with verified backups and authenticated version+commit readback was used separately.
patches.migration: No database change proposed; implementation remains to be designed.
patches.rollback: No implementation to roll back. Retain previous payload and verified pre-update data backups for operational upgrades.
patches.retireWhen: Upstream exact-version service verification works for authenticated instances and passes the same isolation and mismatch cases.

patches.problem: The SSH CLI adapter has no same-turn provider control and queued messages cannot be steered into its running turn.
patches.reason: A config switch alone cannot add a bidirectional provider session, host-owned acknowledgement or trustworthy remote stop evidence while preserving native preparation and routed resources.
patches.owner: Adapter execution owner, queued-message routes and native Codex prepared process boundary
patches.proposal: Opt-in host control with run/company ownership, durable attempt and acknowledgement, phase-spanning deduplication, explicit adapter protocol and preserved native Codex preparation. The companion controlled launcher verifies approved native Codex artifacts and actual provider stop; unsupported or ambiguous ownership still fails closed.
